stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{2 x^{2} + 14 x + 24}{x^{3} + 2 x^{2} - 7 x + 4} \). Determine whether f is continuous at \( x = -4 \). If it is not, classify the discontinuity as removable, a jump, or a vertical asymptote. Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The discontinuity at \( x = -4 \) is removable, because the limit of f(x) there is a finite number.

worked_solution.text: Factor and divide out the common factor: for \( x \ne -4 \), \( f(x) = \frac{2 x + 6}{\left(x - 1\right)^{2}} \).
The reduced expression is continuous at \( x = -4 \), so \( \lim_{x \to -4} f(x) = - \frac{2}{25} \), a finite number, while f(-4) is undefined.
The limit exists but f has no value there, so the discontinuity is removable.

options.label: The discontinuity at \( x = -4 \) is a jump, because f is undefined there so the limit does not exist.
options.derivation: the limit declared nonexistent because f is undefined at the input, so the break called a jump

options.label: There is no discontinuity at \( x = -4 \), because the limits from the left and from the right are equal.
options.derivation: agreeing one sided limits taken as continuity, with the missing value ignored

options.label: The discontinuity at \( x = -4 \) is a vertical asymptote, because the denominator of f is 0 there.
options.derivation: the zero of the original denominator named an asymptote although its factor divides out
